output.reason: Right hand numbness and tingling for a few days, worse at night, without reported weakness, facial droop or speech change, fits a compressive nerve pattern manageable with self-care guidance and a clear escalation trigger.
output.patientMessage: You can start with self-care: avoid sleeping with the wrist bent, try a neutral wrist splint at night, and take breaks from repetitive gripping or wrist movements. Night-worse hand tingling often comes from nerve compression at the wrist. Call 911 if you develop sudden face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking. Message us if you notice hand weakness, dropping objects, constant numbness, or no improvement over the next few weeks.
differential: Carpal tunnel syndrome (median nerve compression at the wrist)
Other peripheral nerve compression, e.g. thoracic outlet or cervical radiculopathy
